title: flags and group have no CLI setter

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`Item.flags` and `Item.group` are real fields with model, render and serialisation
support. `flags` is load-bearing: `sync.exclude_flags` uses it to drop items from the
derived next-pointer. `group` renders as a phase label row above a run of items.

Neither can be set from the CLI. `ops.set_fields` even lists `flags` in its `known` set,
but `cmd_set` never wires an argument for it; `group` is not in `known` at all. Today
both arrive only through `slicer migrate` or `slicer import`, so a project that started
from `slicer add` can never use either.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `--flag` (repeatable, replaces the list like `--tree` does) and `--group` to `set`.
Add `group` to the `known` set. Consider `--no-flags` / `--group ""` for clearing.

**Not in this slice:** add/remove semantics for list fields; `set` replaces, and changing
that is its own decision.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: `slicer set S01 --flag OWNER` then `slicer sync --check` sees the item excluded.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit: `group` into `set_fields` known plus a flag-newline guard (ops),
`--flag`/`--no-flags`/`--group` on `set` (cli), tests in `test_ops.py`.
